Which means that these are the steps I will ideally do this week, though it will likely spill into the next weeks:

1.  create a script that will download the .fasta files directly to hawk
    1.  this cuts out storing them on my machine, its more efficient
    2.  I will be downloading both the genomic and protein fastas as I do not know which to use
2.  At first, the script will only do a few accessions
    1.  this means I can compare genomic fastas that I process through blast p to their protein fastas, if they are the same, then I might as well save the time and use theirs, when I download them all.
3.  Regardless of the results from that mini-experiment, I will set-up a script or some pipeline for turning genomic fastas into protein fastas
    1.  this could still be useful in future, i.e. if Aaron gives me more genomes from Alberto, he wont have the protein fastas, so I might as well already have that pipeline ready
    2.  I will need to decide if I want to do this through bash or R and command line or slurm
4.  I will need to figure out how to store the results of the fasta-downloading script
    1.  i.e. do I do more .rds, would that work on hawk? should it be a list object?
        1.  I think yes to both, but I'll see when I get there

        2.  A good idea is to test that on my machine before doing it on hawk, more visual so I know better what is actually happening
